rows.instruction: Read the information given below and answer the questions that follow.
rows.context:
Kohlrausch observed an interesting pattern between the values of molar conductance at infinite dilution (\(\Lambda^{\infty}_{m}\)) for strong electrolytes. It was observed that different pairs of electrolytes having a common cation or anion had almost same difference of \(\Lambda^{\infty}_{m}\). On the basis of his observation, he postulated a law known as Kohlrausch’s Law of Independent Migration of ions.

The values of molar conductivities at infinite dilution for some cations and anions are as follows:

| Ion | \(\lambda^{\infty}_{m}\) (\(\mathrm{Scm^2mol^{-1}}\)) |
|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}\) | \(127{\cdot}2\) |
| \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\) | \(76{\cdot}3\) |
| \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) | \(119{\cdot}0\) |
| \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\) | \(160{\cdot}0\) |
rows.text: State the Kohlrausch’s Law of Independent Migration of ions.

(b) \(\mathrm{KMnO_4 + H_2SO_4 + FeSO_4 \longrightarrow}\) ____ + ____ + ____ + ____

(Atomic Number of Co = 27 and Zn = 30)

(i) Give *one* example each of fibrous protein and globular protein.
(ii) The structures of two amino acids, glycine and alanine, are given below. Draw the peptide linkage between these two amino acids.

rows.text:

(i) Chlorobenzene is heated with conc. \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) in the presence of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\).
(ii) Ethyl alcohol is treated with \(\mathrm{SOCl_2}\) in the presence of pyridine.
(iii) Chloroform is slowly oxidized with oxygen in the presence of sunlight.

rows.subtopic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction
rows.text:
(i) The rate constant of a first order reaction increases five times when the temperature is raised from 350K to 500K. Calculate the activation energy of the reaction. (\(\mathrm{R} = 8{\cdot}314\ \mathrm{JK^{-1}mol^{-1}}\))
(ii) The unit of rate constant of a reaction is same as that of its rate of reaction. What is the order of this reaction?

(a) The molar conductivity at infinite dilution for \(\lambda^{\infty}_{\mathrm{H^+}} = 348{\cdot}65\ \mathrm{Scm^2mol^{-1}}\) and for \(\lambda^{\infty}_{\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}} = 41{\cdot}4\ \mathrm{Scm^2mol^{-1}}\) respectively.
Calculate the degree of dissociation (\(\alpha\)) of acetic acid if its molar conductivity (\(\Lambda^{c}_{m}\)) is \(40{\cdot}65\ \mathrm{Scm^2mol^{-1}}\).
(b) Compounds [A] and [B] are two electrolytes. Upon dilution, the molar conductivity of compound [A] increases 3 times while that of [B] increases 30 times. Which one of the two is a weak electrolyte? Why?
(c) Can copper sulphate solution be stored in a zinc pot? Give a reason for your answer by referring to the values given below.
\(E^{0}_{\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}} = -0{\cdot}76\,\mathrm{V}\), \(E^{0}_{\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}} = +0{\cdot}34\,\mathrm{V}\)

(a) When a current of \(0{\cdot}75\) ampere is passed through a \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) solution for 25 minutes, \(0{\cdot}370\,\mathrm{g}\) of copper is deposited. Calculate the atomic weight of copper by using the given information.
(b) Two metals A and B have standard reduction potential values, \(-0{\cdot}76\,\mathrm{V}\) and \(+0{\cdot}34\,\mathrm{V}\) respectively.
Which of these metals will liberate \(\mathrm{H_2}\) gas from dil. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)? Why?
(c) Why does the specific conductivity (\(\kappa\)) of a solution decrease on dilution?

Identify the compounds [A], [B] and [C] in the following reactions:
(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br \xrightarrow{KCN} [A] \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} [B] \xrightarrow{HNO_2} [C]}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH \xrightarrow{NH_3} [A] \xrightarrow{\Delta} [B] \xrightarrow{Br_2\,/\,KOH} [C]}\)

rows.subtopic: Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass
rows.text:
(i) Calculate the mass of ascorbic acid (molecular mass \(= 176\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\)) to be dissolved in 75 g of acetic acid to lower its freezing point by \(1{\cdot}5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\). Assume that the solute neither associates nor dissociates in solution.
(\(\mathrm{K_f}\) for acetic acid \(= 3{\cdot}9\ \mathrm{K\ kg\ mol^{-1}}\))
(ii) A solution of an organic compound was prepared by dissolving \(6{\cdot}8\,\mathrm{g}\) in \(0{\cdot}1\) litre of water. Calculate the osmotic pressure of this solution at \(25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\).
(Molecular mass of organic compound \(= 321{\cdot}45\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\))
(iii) Why are aquatic species more comfortable in cold water than warm water?

rows.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
rows.text:
(i) What happens when (write chemical equations):
(a) Calcium acetate is subjected to dry distillation.
(b) Acetaldehyde is reduced with hydrogen in the presence of \(\mathrm{Zn\,/\,Hg}\) and conc. \(\mathrm{HCl}\).
(c) Acetic acid is heated with ethyl alcohol in the presence of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\).
(ii) An organic compound [X] with molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_4O}\) forms compound [Y] on oxidation. Compound [X] undergoes haloform reaction. On treatment with \(\mathrm{HCN}\), compound [X] forms a product [Z] which on hydrolysis gives 2-hydroxy propanoic acid.
(a) Write down the structures of compounds [X] and [Y].
(b) Name the product formed when [X] reacts with dil. \(\mathrm{NaOH}\).

(a) With reference to Valence Bond Theory (VBT), answer the following questions regarding the complex ion \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\).
(1) What is the oxidation number of chromium in the complex?
(2) State the magnetic behaviour of the complex.
(3) How many unpaired electrons are there in the complex?
(4) State the type of hybridisation of the central metal atom.
(b) The coordination complex \(\mathrm{CoNO_2Cl.5NH_3}\) exists in two isomeric forms ‘P’ and ‘Q’. Isomer ‘P’ reacts with \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\) solution to give white precipitate whereas ‘Q’ does not give any precipitate with \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\) solution.
(1) Write the structural formula of isomers ‘P’ and ‘Q’.
(2) Name the type of isomerism involved.
(c) Explain why an aqueous solution of potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II) does not give the test of ferrous ion.

(a) Write the electronic configuration of the following:
(1) \(\mathrm{d^4}\) (high spin octahedral)
(2) \(\mathrm{d^6}\) (low spin octahedral)
(b) Based on the above configuration, calculate the value of Crystal Field Splitting Energy (CFSE). (Ignore pairing energy)
(c) Name the type of isomerism exhibited by the following pairs of coordination compounds.
(1) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(ONO)]Cl_2}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5NO_2]Cl_2}\)
(2) \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(NH_3)_4]Br_2}\) and \(\mathrm{[PtBr_2(NH_3)_4]Cl_2}\)
(d) Which of the following coordination complexes is an outer orbital complex? Explain.
\(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\) or \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}\)
